summary: The agent implemented most of the configurable collection feature, but failed both suites: 30 baseline regressions and 2 new-test failures. The dominant issue is that its collection-assignment changes alter existing factory handling and generated variable naming; it also omits object-factory precedence for stream results despite that being explicit in the prompt.
quick_failure_summary: Collection assignment changes regress existing mappings, and configured stream mappings construct the selected implementation instead of using an applicable object factory.

details.reasoning: The baseline JUnit report records 30 failures in existing tests. Four Issue1131 failures show that the expected collection object factory is no longer invoked. In CollectionAssignmentBuilder, the agent replaces the existing factoryMethod argument with configuredFactoryMethod, which is null for ordinary non-configured mappings. The other 26 Issue913 fixture failures result from moving instance-variable allocation into the common collection wrapper, reserving names even when the new variable is unused and changing generated source identifiers such as set to set1. These are direct regressions in files modified by the agent, so FAIL_REGRESSION takes precedence. Separately, both new failures show stream mappings returning ChosenList instead of FactoryList because the agent did not update StreamMappingMethod.ftl to force factory-aware materialization.
details.secondary_factors: The agent's focused suite covered configured stream construction and non-stream factories, but not the explicitly required combination of configured stream results with an applicable object factory. It also did not run the full baseline suite, so the existing Issue1131 and Issue913 regressions went undetected.

problem_assessment.notes: The task is broad and requires processor lifecycle handling, Java properties parsing, type-system validation, construction-path integration, streams, direct bean properties, and factory precedence. The failed stream behavior is explicitly covered by the sentence that the rule applies to stream materialization and that an applicable object factory still wins. The reference solution demonstrates the task is solvable, and the test failures are stable assertion or generated-source comparison failures rather than flaky behavior.

evidence: The trajectory shows the agent successfully ran processor verification and a focused 152-test suite with zero failures, so dependencies and the Java/Maven toolchain were operational.

The new JUnit report executed all 53 hidden tests and produced two ordinary assertion failures in shouldGiveObjectFactoriesPrecedenceForStreams rather than bootstrap, import, or infrastructure errors.

The baseline JUnit failures exercise agent-modified collection assignment code: Issue1131 loses a collection factory invocation, and Issue913 generated-source fixtures show systematic variable renaming.
Although the post-agent log notes a three-way test.patch merge failure, the wrapper recovered, ran the full classified suites, and generated structured results for 3641 baseline and 53 new tests.
environment_assessment.finding: No meaningful external blocker was found; the verifier recovered from its patch-merge hiccup and the observed failures are explained by the implementation changes.
